title: add-curation-heatmap-and-release-teaser-cards-for-model-intake
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Introduce a curation heatmap that surfaces onboarding signals (coverage, perf delta, safety flags) and a small service that generates concise release teaser cards for changelogs. Enables faster triage and more informative release notes. No API breaking changes.
description:
Motivation: As the number of onboarded model candidates grows, reviewers need a compact, visual summary of where a model stands across signal dimensions (performance, cost, safety, sample coverage) and a way to surface the most relevant changes in release notes. This PR adds two pieces: (1) a curation heatmap generator that aggregates onboarding telemetry into tile scores, and (2) a release-teaser generator that synthesizes 1-2 line 'teaser' cards used in changelogs and release drafts. Changeset: - telemetry/curation_heatmap.py: heatmap aggregation and scoring engine (configurable weights) - telemetry/fixtures/sample_intake.json: small sample for unit tests and local dev - services/release_teaser/service.py: heuristics that convert profile deltas into teaser text templates - ui/components/CurationHeatmap.vue: frontend tile grid + legend - docs/curation/heatmap.md: usage, tuning knobs, and examples - tests/test_heatmap.py, tests/test_release_teaser.py: unit + integration tests Note: description is intentionally compact; see changed_files and commits for more detail. Checklist: - [x] Aggregation and scoring; weight config - [x] Unit tests for edge cases (no telemetry, partial metrics) - [x] End-to-end smoke test (local fixture) - [x] Basic component for Console (static data binding) - [x] Release notes generator implemented and integrated with draft pipeline Rollout: feature gated behind `curation_heatmap` FF. Start with internal rollout for model-review team, then flip for all curators after 2 weeks of usage metrics. Backout: revert FF and remove teaser consumer if false positives in teaser generation are reported.

Technical notes: Heatmap tiles compute a normalized score in [0,1] per dimension: perf_delta (lower is better -> inverted), cost_change (lower better), safety_flags (count scaled), sample_coverage (fraction). A weighted sum yields a 'priority' score used to dim/highlight tiles. Release teaser heuristics: prefer perf deltas > 5% or coverage increases > 10% or newly triggered safety gates. Teaser text is deterministic and templated to avoid hallucinations.

Why unique: This PR focuses on curator UX (visual+text summary) rather than raw profiling or changelog automation. It bridges telemetry->UI->release-notes with conservative heuristics and a feature flag for safe rollout.
